stem: Sunita invests Rs 50,000 in a fixed deposit. For the first 2 years the bank compounds interest at 10% per annum; for the next 3 years the rate changes to 12% per annum. What is the total amount at the end of 5 years? [Given: (1.10)^2 = 1.21 and (1.12)^3 = 1.404928]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Rs 80,525.50 = 50000 x (1.10)^5 applies the first-phase rate of 10% for all 5 years, ignoring that the rate changes to 12% after Year 2; the rate-period combination is mismatched.
A rate change partitions the timeline into phases; the output of each phase becomes the input principal of the next, so you chain the multiplications rather than averaging or adding.
Rs 88,117 = 50000 x (1.12)^5 applies the second-phase rate of 12% for all 5 years, ignoring that the first 2 years earned 10%; the formula is applied to the full horizon at the wrong rate.
Rs 78,000 = 50000 + 50000 x (0.10 x 2 + 0.12 x 3) computes simple interest for each phase and adds them together, treating both phases as SI instead of CI; the compounding is entirely dropped.

explanation_sections.punchline: A rate change partitions the timeline into phases; the output of each phase becomes the input principal of the next, so you chain the multiplications rather than averaging or adding.
explanation_sections.approach: Phase 1 (Years 1-2): A1 = 50000 x (1.10)^2 = 50000 x 1.21 = 60500. Phase 2 (Years 3-5): A2 = A1 x (1.12)^3 = 60500 x 1.404928 = 84998.14. The Rs 60,500 is the bridge linking the two phases.
explanation_sections.lesson: Two-phase problems require exactly two multiplications chained. Never average the rates or apply a single multi-year factor across the full period at one rate.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds: one multiplication per phase plus one chain. Trap is option 1 (first-phase rate extended to 5 years), the most natural mistake when students stop after Phase 1 and use n = 5.
